newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso soft on Finmin brother's slaying.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso soft on Finmin brother's slaying.

text.p: The Mexican peso opened weaker across the board Monday as foreign players speculated in the wake of news that Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz's brother was shot to death Saturday night, dealers said.
"The peso is under pressure from the killing, but the market may calm down later," a dealer said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour counterpart began the session 1.5 and 1.6 centavos weaker, respectively, at 7.7755/7.7800 and 7.7740/7.7770 per dollar.
Same-day peso contracts had meanwhile opened 2.2 centavos weaker at 7.7690/7.7740 per dollar.

Alejandro Ortiz, brother of Finance Minister Ortiz, was shot and killed Saturday evening in an apparent street crime after he had parked his car outside his home in a posh section of Mexico City. Police said they are treating the crime as a robbery, though no valuables have been discovered missing.
The speculation on the peso revolved around concerns the killing may have been politically motivated, though no evidence for this has emerged so far.
Dealers said stronger than expected GDP data released shortly before trade opened, coupled with firm U.S. stocks and bond markets could bolster the peso in late trade.
"They brought forward the GDP release by a day, which was the big news we were expecting this week," the trader added.
The Finance Ministry announced GDP for the second quarter had risen by 8.8 percent from the same quarter last year. The market had looked for a rise of around 5.92 percent.
Traders predicted a dealing range of 7.7600/7.7900 per dollar for the 48-hour peso.
